speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; please tell me about your specific symptoms or any concerns you have as a newborn.

To start, has your baby had any trouble feeding, breathing, or have you noticed any unusual colors like jaundice or blue tinting?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Since the mother had no prenatal care, were there any specific complications during delivery, such as prolonged rupture of membranes, chorioamnionitis, or meconium staining? Also, has the baby shown signs of sepsis like temperature instability, lethargy, or a poor feeding history?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a PDA), bluish non-blanching macules (petechiae or purpura), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and hearing loss in a newborn with no immunization history is classic for this diagnosis. I will confirm the diagnosis once you provide the results of the newborn screening for rubella IgM.
